k: The east bridge ends in nothing. Far, far below, through the violet haze, something glitters — another shard, maybe. Maybe a whole country, falling slower than you.
src: 'The east bridge ends in nothing. Far, far below, through the violet haze, something glitters — another shard, maybe. Maybe a whole country, falling slower than you.'

k: A doorframe with no house behind it. Somebody has hung a wreath of wire and rag flowers on it, and swept the step.
src: 'A doorframe with no house behind it. Somebody has hung a wreath of wire and rag flowers on it, and swept the step.'

k: The common soup pot. It smells of ash and onion and, faintly, of hope. Mostly ash.
src: 'The common soup pot. It smells of ash and onion and, faintly, of hope. Mostly ash.'

k: When I'm better, I'm going to be a Vanguard. Like Wren.
src: 'When I\'m better, I\'m going to be a Vanguard. Like Wren.'

k: Ilse says I can be anything. She said it like she was cross about it.
src: 'Ilse says I can be anything. She said it like she was cross about it.'

k: ...Wren? You're real? I thought the rot was making me see things again.
src: '...Wren? You\'re real? I thought the rot was making me see things again.'

k: Everybody from home is gone except me and Ilse. Ilse says that makes us family. She says it angry, but I think she means it.
src: 'Everybody from home is gone except me and Ilse. Ilse says that makes us family. She says it angry, but I think she means it.'

k: She's doing better. The Ward Mother sat with her all last night. She sits with everyone, one night each, in turn.
src: 'She\'s doing better. The Ward Mother sat with her all last night. She sits with everyone, one night each, in turn.'

k: I don't know when she sleeps. I don't think she knows either.
src: 'I don\'t know when she sleeps. I don\'t think she knows either.'

k: My hand's pink again. Pink! I've never been so happy to look like a boiled ham.
src: 'My hand\'s pink again. Pink! I\'ve never been so happy to look like a boiled ham.'

k: Cut my hand on a scrap of the old Cathedral. A _holy_ scrap. Didn't help.
src: 'Cut my hand on a scrap of the old Cathedral. A _holy_ scrap. Didn\'t help.'

k: Ward Mother says the violet's stopped at my wrist. She says it like a promise. She doesn't make promises.
src: 'Ward Mother says the violet\'s stopped at my wrist. She says it like a promise. She doesn\'t make promises.'

k: That girl with the bun? Ilse? She held my hand while my Tam went. Didn't say anything. Didn't need to.
src: 'That girl with the bun? Ilse? She held my hand while my Tam went. Didn\'t say anything. Didn\'t need to.'

k: You're the one she won't look at. I've been watching. Whatever you did, girl — she still knows exactly where you're standing, every second.
src: 'You\'re the one she won\'t look at. I\'ve been watching. Whatever you did, girl — she still knows exactly where you\'re standing, every second.'

k: The wall
src: 'The wall'

k: A cauldron of boiling bandages. Ilse's labels on every jar nearby, in the same tiny, exact handwriting you remember. One says: DO NOT. EVER. — I.M.
src: 'A cauldron of boiling bandages. Ilse\'s labels on every jar nearby, in the same tiny, exact handwriting you remember. One says: DO NOT. EVER. — I.M.'

k: Shelves of empty phial-racks. Someone has counted them in chalk: 2. Then the 2 is crossed out: 1.
src: 'Shelves of empty phial-racks. Someone has counted them in chalk: 2. Then the 2 is crossed out: 1.'

k: Shelves stacked with sunsalt phials, glowing like coals. Someone has written a new number in chalk, and underlined it twice.
src: 'Shelves stacked with sunsalt phials, glowing like coals. Someone has written a new number in chalk, and underlined it twice.'

k: The Ward Mother? In _my_ chapel? Sit, sit. I'll not take her coin. Yours, though.
src: 'The Ward Mother? In _my_ chapel? Sit, sit. I\'ll not take her coin. Yours, though.'

k: A pew to sleep on and a bowl of something hot. Hundred and twenty. We used to be a chapel; now we're a mercy with a bar.
src: 'A pew to sleep on and a bowl of something hot. Hundred and twenty. We used to be a chapel; now we\'re a mercy with a bar.'

k: the Last Bell
src: 'the Last Bell'

k: I cast bells. Forty years. Every bell in this city, I could tell you its voice blindfolded.
src: 'I cast bells. Forty years. Every bell in this city, I could tell you its voice blindfolded.'

k: Now I cast spoons. Spoons don't sing. But you can't eat soup with a bell, can you? Can you. I've tried.
src: 'Now I cast spoons. Spoons don\'t sing. But you can\'t eat soup with a bell, can you? Can you. I\'ve tried.'

k: There's a sellsword at Kiteholm loses every hand on purpose so the orphans can eat. Or he's just that bad.
src: 'There\'s a sellsword at Kiteholm loses every hand on purpose so the orphans can eat. Or he\'s just that bad.'

k: Either way, I'd like to play him.
src: 'Either way, I\'d like to play him.'

k: Shh. I'm bluffing. I've been bluffing for a year. About everything.
src: 'Shh. I\'m bluffing. I\'ve been bluffing for a year. About everything.'

k: A broken pillar from the old chapel. Someone has carved a tally of every day since the Sundering. The count stopped at 300 and started over at 1, in a different hand.
src: 'A broken pillar from the old chapel. Someone has carved a tally of every day since the Sundering. The count stopped at 300 and started over at 1, in a different hand.'

k: Sluice wheel
src: 'Sluice wheel'

k: Sluice gate
src: 'Sluice gate'

k: Cracked wall
src: 'Cracked wall'

k: Alcove
src: 'Alcove'

k: Notes
src: 'Notes'

k: Cages. Small ones — child-sized. Every door hangs open. Whatever was inside left, or was let out, or was used.
src: 'Cages. Small ones — child-sized. Every door hangs open. Whatever was inside left, or was let out, or was used.'

k: A drowned order of service, the ink run to violet: "VESPERS EVE. The Under-Choir shall descend to the Cistern and hold the Reflected Note until the Precentor's signal. Do not stop for any reason. — By order of the Hierophant."
src: 'A drowned order of service, the ink run to violet: "VESPERS EVE. The Under-Choir shall descend to the Cistern and hold the Reflected Note until the Precentor\'s signal. Do not stop for any reason. — By order of the Hierophant."'

k: Hymnals, swollen fat with water. One has fallen open to a page where somebody has written in the margin, very small: _I don't want to sing this one._
src: 'Hymnals, swollen fat with water. One has fallen open to a page where somebody has written in the margin, very small: _I don\'t want to sing this one._'

k: A reliquary statue of a Keeper holding up a lantern. Something large has rubbed against it so often that one side is polished to a shine.
src: 'A reliquary statue of a Keeper holding up a lantern. Something large has rubbed against it so often that one side is polished to a shine.'

k: A little statue of Saint Aurel, patron of tuners, still dry. Someone left a candle stub at her feet. It is not very old.
src: 'A little statue of Saint Aurel, patron of tuners, still dry. Someone left a candle stub at her feet. It is not very old.'

k: A pillar carved with a high-water mark from two hundred years ago. The water today is three hands higher.
src: 'A pillar carved with a high-water mark from two hundred years ago. The water today is three hands higher.'

k: A great bronze bell, sunk to its shoulder. Its rim is engraved: _I CALL THE LIVING. I MOURN THE DEAD. I BREAK THE LIGHTNING._ It has done none of these things in a year.
src: 'A great bronze bell, sunk to its shoulder. Its rim is engraved: _I CALL THE LIVING. I MOURN THE DEAD. I BREAK THE LIGHTNING._ It has done none of these things in a year.'

k: Vestry shelves. Choir robes hang in rows, dripping. There are exactly as many empty hooks as there are singers in the Loft.
src: 'Vestry shelves. Choir robes hang in rows, dripping. There are exactly as many empty hooks as there are singers in the Loft.'

k: A bellwright's anvil, carried all the way down here for repairs. The tools are laid out neatly, as if the smith only stepped away.
src: 'A bellwright\'s anvil, carried all the way down here for repairs. The tools are laid out neatly, as if the smith only stepped away.'

k: My barge goes back down when the ember-wind turns. Which is whenever it likes.
src: 'My barge goes back down when the ember-wind turns. Which is whenever it likes.'

k: You'll hate it up here. Then you'll never leave. Then you'll leave anyway, because that's what people like you do.
src: 'You\'ll hate it up here. Then you\'ll never leave. Then you\'ll leave anyway, because that\'s what people like you do.'

k: You saved my Kites. Everything's the same price, because I'm poor, but I'll _feel_ generous at you.
src: 'You saved my Kites. Everything\'s the same price, because I\'m poor, but I\'ll _feel_ generous at you.'

k: Scrap and Sundry! If it fell off something, I sell it. If it didn't fall off something, give it time.
src: 'Scrap and Sundry! If it fell off something, I sell it. If it didn\'t fall off something, give it time.'

k: Scrap-picker. I go down the ropes for metal. The Baron weighs it. The Baron's scale is a liar.
src: 'Scrap-picker. I go down the ropes for metal. The Baron weighs it. The Baron\'s scale is a liar.'

k: Don't go down the Underhang without rope. Don't go down with rope either. Just — don't.
src: 'Don\'t go down the Underhang without rope. Don\'t go down with rope either. Just — don\'t.'

k: Saw the Boss flying a kite up here. Laughing like a gull.
src: 'Saw the Boss flying a kite up here. Laughing like a gull.'

k: Been waiting a year to hear that. Didn't know I was waiting till I heard it.
src: 'Been waiting a year to hear that. Didn\'t know I was waiting till I heard it.'

k: Flew kites on the Gale Coast sixty years. Now the whole world's the sky, and I'm still flying kites.
src: 'Flew kites on the Gale Coast sixty years. Now the whole world\'s the sky, and I\'m still flying kites.'

k: Wind's honest. Wind doesn't promise you noon forever. It just blows.
src: 'Wind\'s honest. Wind doesn\'t promise you noon forever. It just blows.'

k: I wash for the whole shard. Ash in everything. You get used to gray.
src: 'I wash for the whole shard. Ash in everything. You get used to gray.'

k: The Boss brings me the Kites' things once a week. Folded. He folds them. Twelve years old and he _folds_.
src: 'The Boss brings me the Kites\' things once a week. Folded. He folds them. Twelve years old and he _folds_.'

k: The Baron says he was always going to send us. He was getting his boots on. Big boots. Took a while.
src: 'The Baron says he was always going to send us. He was getting his boots on. Big boots. Took a while.'

k: Baron's terrace. Baron's air. You're breathing it, so technically you owe him.
src: 'Baron\'s terrace. Baron\'s air. You\'re breathing it, so technically you owe him.'

k: I'm joking. Mostly. He's got a ledger for breaths.
src: 'I\'m joking. Mostly. He\'s got a ledger for breaths.'

k: They came, and they didn't get one. Not one Kite. My Fig is asleep in the Nest with her boots on.
src: 'They came, and they didn\'t get one. Not one Kite. My Fig is asleep in the Nest with her boots on.'

k: Thank you. Whoever you are. Thank you.
src: 'Thank you. Whoever you are. Thank you.'

k: My girl's a Kite. I'm not allowed in the Nest. Boss's rule: no grown-ups.
src: 'My girl\'s a Kite. I\'m not allowed in the Nest. Boss\'s rule: no grown-ups.'

k: I'm not angry. When the raiders took Skerry's boy, nobody grown went after him. Pip did.
src: 'I\'m not angry. When the raiders took Skerry\'s boy, nobody grown went after him. Pip did.'

k: I saw him. On the Gallows Shard, before they cut it loose. Black armor. A mask that weeps.
src: 'I saw him. On the Gallows Shard, before they cut it loose. Black armor. A mask that weeps.'

k: He held his sword high, like a man waiting for permission. He never got it. He swung anyway.
src: 'He held his sword high, like a man waiting for permission. He never got it. He swung anyway.'

k: I'm a messenger Kite. I run messages. Mostly the message is "Boss says no."
src: 'I\'m a messenger Kite. I run messages. Mostly the message is "Boss says no."'
